alice: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel selection change we are seeing more batch fragmentation when routing across multi-variant compat sets. 95th p50 latency spiked on a few hosts. Noticed heavy small-batch tail and KV cache miss rate rising.

ben: Oof. Which kernel change specifically? the index-merge path or the fused-attn fallback?

alice: fused-attn preference was flipped for a subset of Llama2-variants to use int8 path. Patch landed: `select_kernel_preference(v) -> prefer_fused_if_quantized=true`.

carla: That could change execution time per-token distribution and break our continuous-batcher heuristics (they assume similar per-variant token throughput). If throughput diverges, the coalescer splits earlier.

david: Can you paste a profiler trace and the queue shape from last night? I want to see bucket counts and token budget exhaustion.

alice: Paste:
```
2026-03-15T03:04:12Z host-17 kernel=fused-int8 model=llama2-v3 variant=B seq=1024 batch=3 duration_per_token=5.8ms kv_cache_hit=false
2026-03-15T03:04:12Z host-17 kernel=matmul-fp16 model=llama2-v3 variant=A seq=64 batch=16 duration_per_token=1.1ms kv_cache_hit=true
queue_shape: [t0:12,t1:3,t2:1] token_budget=1024 active_batches=8
```

maya: Interesting — variant B slows tokens ~5x and also has lower KV hit (cold path). Combined with routing mixing A+B, the batcher is forming many small batches waiting for slow sequences and starving fast ones -> fragmentation.

carla: Two levers to test quickly: 1) compat-aware queue weighting (prefer grouping identical kernel/variant where possible), 2) token_budget per-compat-set instead of global. Both are low-risk config flips.

ben: Also look at warmup: KV misses for B indicate cold cache after fallback routing. Could be that fallback directs to different pool with empty prefix cache. Add explicit KV warmup for canaries.

alice: I tried a quick patch to prefer grouping by kernel fingerprint in the batcher. Latency tail dropped in a 30m canary on host-17 but overall throughput slightly down (more serialization). Logs: `batch_merge_skipped=42 group_pref_score=0.72`.

david: We should quantify cost tradeoff. More grouping reduces fragmentation but may increase queueing latency for some requests. Want to run microbench: 1) baseline continuous batching, 2) kernel-grouping, 3) compat-token-buckets. Use the `batch-bench` tool with these flags: `./tools/batch-bench --policy continuous --group-by kernel --token-bucket 512`.

infra-bot: Scheduled job `batch-bench/mv-routing-experiment` started. Job id: jb-20260315-17.

maya: Also add an experiment for token budget targets that adapt per-variant proportionally to observed per-token cost. E.g. target_token_budget[v] = base_token_budget * (cost_per_token[v] / median_cost). Should avoid hard cuts.

carla: Agree. And ensure compat-set selection honors fallback policy: if a high-cost variant is chosen as fallback, promote cheaper variant shadowing (serve cheaper variant in parallel and fallback output if quality diff small).

ben: Quick idea: augment routing metadata with `expected_token_ms` and let scheduler use that for batch formation heuristic. Then batcher can prefer grouping by similar expected_token_ms ranges (e.g., 0-2ms, 2-5ms, 5ms+).

alice: Ran profiler with `--emit-kv-hits` and saw pattern: many short sequences (<=64) with high KV hit mix with a few long requests that are slow and cold. Those long cold requests are the fragmentation sources.

david: Action items:
- alice: run the three microbench variants and upload results to /tmp/mv-batch-experiments (include p50/p95/p99, throughput, token-cost).
- ben: implement lightweight `expected_token_ms` tag in routing metadata and add comparator in batcher (prefer similar ms).
- carla: prototype per-compat-set token buckets and the bucket refill policy.
- maya: craft canary that restricts fallback routing for 2h to measure KV warmup impact.

alice: Putting numbers in thread once bench completes. For triage, tentative rollback window at 2026-03-16 01:00 if regression persists.

ben: If bench shows kernel-grouping wins p95 without big impact on p50, we can flip as config for dedicated pools only first.

carla: Also need a longer-term fix: kernel selection should publish a throughput profile so routing and batcher can make informed choices. Filing a follow-up RFC after triage.

alice: RFC ack. I'll drop the bench results here in ~2h.

infra-bot: Job `batch-bench/mv-routing-experiment` finished. Results uploaded: s3://redwood-internal/bench/mv-routing/2026-03-15-17/results.json

alice: Uploaded summary: p95 baseline=420ms, p95 group-by-kernel=260ms, p50 baseline=120ms, p50 group-by-kernel=140ms, throughput diff -6%. Will attach raw.

maya: Those look promising. Next step: run canary with group-by-kernel enabled on 10% of traffic and token-bucket adaptive on same cohort.

david: Agree. Rollout plan: canary 10% (2h), monitor p95, KV-hit, batch-size distribution. If p95 improves and throughput impact <10%, promote.

ben: I'll open quick PR for `expected_token_ms` tag and add metric emit.

carla: I'll open PR for per-compat token-buckets with a flag `compat_token_buckets=true` and default off.

alice: Thanks all, will coordinate canary schedule with SRE.

ben: :thumbsup:

carla: :+1:

maya: Thanks — ping me when canary is live and I'll monitor KV warmup dashboards.

alice: closing loop when canary done.
